p2.t: Describe a person who has influenced you.
p2.vi: Tả một người đã ảnh hưởng tới bạn.
b: and explain how they have influenced you
p3: What qualities make someone a good role model?
Phẩm chất nào làm nên một hình mẫu tốt?
Do young people today have different role models from in the past?
Giới trẻ ngày nay có hình mẫu khác ngày xưa không?
Should famous people be expected to behave well in public?
Người nổi tiếng có phải cư xử tốt nơi công cộng không?
p2.m: I'd like to talk about my high school maths teacher, Mr Hung, who probably influenced me more than anyone outside my family. I was in his class for three years, from the age of fifteen to eighteen. At first I didn't like him very much, because he was quite strict and he gave us a lot of homework. But gradually I realised that he really cared about his students. He used to stay after school, without being paid, to help anyone who was struggling, and he always explained things in several different ways until everyone understood. What influenced me most, though, was his attitude to mistakes. Whenever I got something wrong, he would say that a mistake was just information, not a failure. Before I met him, I was afraid of making mistakes, so I often didn't even try difficult problems. Because of him, I became much more confident, and I think that's why I later chose to study engineering. Even now, when I face a difficult task at work, I remember what he told us and I try to treat problems as something to learn from rather than something to be afraid of.

p2.t: Describe a place you visited that you would like to go back to.
p2.vi: Tả một nơi bạn từng đến và muốn quay lại.
b: and explain why you would like to go back
p3: Why do people like to travel to new places?
Vì sao người ta thích đi nơi mới?
What are the effects of tourism on local communities?
Du lịch ảnh hưởng thế nào tới cộng đồng địa phương?
Will people travel more or less in the future?
Tương lai người ta sẽ đi du lịch nhiều hơn hay ít hơn?
p2.m: I'd like to talk about Da Lat, a city in the Central Highlands of Vietnam, which I visited with my university friends about three years ago. We went there in December, just after our exams, so we were all in a very relaxed mood. Da Lat is quite different from the rest of the country, because it's high up in the mountains and the weather is cool all year round. We stayed in a small guest house surrounded by pine trees. During the day we rented motorbikes and rode out to waterfalls and flower farms, and in the evenings we walked around the night market, eating grilled rice paper and drinking hot soy milk. One morning we got up at five o'clock to watch the sunrise over the valley, which was absolutely beautiful, although it was freezing. The reason I'd like to go back is partly the peaceful atmosphere. My life in Ho Chi Minh City is very busy and noisy, and in Da Lat I felt that I could finally breathe. But it's also because of the memories. Some of those friends now live abroad, so if we could all go back together one day, it would be really special.

p2.t: Describe a skill you learned that you think is useful.
p2.vi: Tả một kỹ năng bạn đã học và thấy hữu ích.
b: when and how you learned it
and explain why it is useful
p3: Which skills are most important for young people today?
Kỹ năng nào quan trọng nhất với giới trẻ ngày nay?
Is it better to learn skills at school or at work?
Học kỹ năng ở trường hay ở chỗ làm tốt hơn?
Will machines replace people in skilled jobs?
Máy móc có thay người trong việc cần tay nghề không?
p2.m: The skill I'd like to describe is cooking, which I learned when I moved away from home to study at university. Before that, my mother always cooked for the family, so I could only make instant noodles. When I started living alone, I realised that eating out every day was too expensive and not very healthy, so I decided to teach myself. At first I watched cooking videos online and called my mother almost every evening to ask how to make simple dishes like fried rice or soup. It was quite difficult at the beginning. I burned quite a few meals, and once I put far too much salt in a fish dish and had to throw it away. But gradually I got better, and after about six months I could cook most of the traditional dishes my family eats. I think it's a really useful skill for several reasons. First, it saves a lot of money. Second, I know exactly what's in my food, so I eat more healthily. And finally, it's a great way to bring people together. These days I often invite friends over for dinner, and cooking for them makes me feel proud and happy.

p2.t: Describe a book or film that made you think.
p2.vi: Tả một cuốn sách hoặc bộ phim khiến bạn suy nghĩ.
b: when you read or saw it
and explain why it made you think
p3: Do people read less than they used to?
Người ta có đọc ít hơn trước không?
Should films be used to teach history?
Có nên dùng phim để dạy lịch sử không?
How has technology changed the way we enjoy stories?
Công nghệ đã đổi cách ta thưởng thức câu chuyện thế nào?
p2.m: I'm going to talk about a film called Parasite, a South Korean film that I watched in the cinema a few years ago, after it won several international awards. It's about two families: a poor family who live in a small basement apartment and a very rich family who live in a beautiful modern house. The poor family gradually find jobs working for the rich family, by pretending they don't know each other, and the story becomes more and more tense until it ends quite violently. At first I thought it was going to be a comedy, because the beginning is very funny. But the longer I watched, the more uncomfortable I felt. The film made me think about inequality, and about how people from different social classes can live in the same city but have completely different lives. What really stayed with me was a scene where it rains heavily. For the rich family, the rain is just an inconvenience that spoils their plans, but for the poor family it floods their home and they lose everything. After the film, my friends and I talked about it for hours, and I still think about that scene whenever there's a big storm.

p2.t: Describe an important change in your life.
p2.vi: Tả một thay đổi quan trọng trong đời bạn.
b: and explain why it was important
p3: Why do some people find change difficult?
Vì sao có người thấy thay đổi là khó?
Is it better to change jobs often or stay in one job?
Đổi việc thường xuyên hay ở một chỗ tốt hơn?
How have cities in your country changed in recent years?
Các thành phố ở nước bạn thay đổi thế nào gần đây?
p2.m: An important change in my life happened about two years ago, when I left my job at a bank and started working for a small technology company. I had worked at the bank for nearly five years, and it was a secure job with a good salary, so it wasn't an easy decision. However, I had started to feel bored, because I was doing the same tasks every day and I didn't feel that I was learning anything new. When a friend told me that his company was looking for someone to manage customer projects, I decided to apply, and to my surprise I got the job. To be honest, I was very nervous at first. My salary was a little lower, and I had to learn a lot of new skills very quickly, such as using project management software and talking to clients in English. There were several weeks when I wondered if I'd made a mistake. But after a few months, I started to really enjoy it. The change was important because it showed me that I could adapt to something new, and it gave me much more confidence. I also feel that my work is more meaningful now, because I can see the results of what I do.

p2.t: Describe a time when you helped someone.
p2.vi: Tả một lần bạn giúp ai đó.
b: and explain how you felt afterwards
p3: Why do some people volunteer to help others?
Vì sao có người tình nguyện giúp người khác?
Should schools teach children to help in the community?
Trường có nên dạy trẻ giúp cộng đồng không?
Are people less helpful in big cities than in small towns?
Người ở thành phố lớn có ít giúp nhau hơn ở thị trấn nhỏ không?
p2.m: I'd like to describe a time when I helped an elderly neighbour of mine, Mrs Lan, who lives alone in the flat next to mine. Last year, during the rainy season, she slipped on the wet stairs and broke her wrist. Her children live in another city, so for about two months she had real difficulty doing everyday things like shopping and cooking. When I found out what had happened, I offered to help. Every few days I went to the market for her and carried her shopping upstairs, and on Sundays I usually cooked a little extra food and took it round to her. I also went with her to the hospital a couple of times for check-ups, because she was nervous about taking a taxi on her own. It didn't take much of my time, but it obviously meant a lot to her. She often told me stories about the neighbourhood when she was young, which I found really interesting. Afterwards, I felt very happy and also a bit surprised, because I realised that I had been living next to her for three years without really knowing her. Now we're good friends, and she always gives me fruit from her family's garden.

p2.t: Describe a piece of technology you use every day.
p2.vi: Tả một thiết bị công nghệ bạn dùng hằng ngày.
b: and explain how your life would be different without it
p3: Has technology made people's lives easier or more stressful?
Công nghệ làm đời sống dễ hơn hay căng thẳng hơn?
Should children be allowed to use smartphones?
Có nên cho trẻ dùng điện thoại thông minh?
What technology do you think will be important in the future?
Bạn nghĩ công nghệ nào sẽ quan trọng sau này?
p2.m: The piece of technology I use every day is my laptop. I bought it about four years ago, when I started my first full-time job, and it's become an essential part of my life. I use it mainly for work. I'm a graphic designer, so I spend most of the day creating images, editing photos and sending files to clients. But I also use it for lots of other things. In the evenings I watch films or online courses, I video-call my parents, who live in another province, and at weekends I use it to plan trips and manage my money. Without my laptop, my life would be very different. First of all, I simply couldn't do my job, because all the software I need runs on a computer. I'd probably have to work in an office every day instead of working from home sometimes, which I really appreciate. I'd also find it harder to keep learning new skills, because most of the courses I take are online. On the other hand, I sometimes think I might be healthier without it, because I'd spend less time sitting down and looking at a screen, so maybe it would be good for me to switch it off a bit more often.

p2.t: Describe a goal you would like to achieve in the future.
p2.vi: Tả một mục tiêu bạn muốn đạt trong tương lai.
b: what you need to do to achieve it
and explain why it is important to you
p3: Is it important to set goals in life?
Đặt mục tiêu trong đời có quan trọng không?
Do young people today have more opportunities than their parents had?
Giới trẻ ngày nay có nhiều cơ hội hơn bố mẹ họ không?
Should success be measured by money?
Có nên đo thành công bằng tiền không?
p2.m: One goal I'd really like to achieve is to get a master's degree in environmental science from a university abroad. I decided on this about a year ago, after I worked as a volunteer on a project to clean up a polluted river in my hometown. It made me realise how serious environmental problems are in my country, and I'd like to have the knowledge to do something about them. To achieve this goal, there are several things I need to do. The first is to improve my English, because most universities require an IELTS score of at least 6.5, so at the moment I'm studying for the test every evening. I also need to save money, since studying abroad is very expensive, although I'm also going to apply for scholarships. And finally, I need to get more experience in the field, so I'm hoping to find a job with an environmental organisation next year. This goal is important to me because I want my work to make a real difference. I think young people today will have to deal with the effects of climate change for the rest of their lives, so it's something I want to understand properly and help to solve.

p2.t: Describe a celebration or festival you enjoyed.
p2.vi: Tả một lễ hội hoặc dịp ăn mừng bạn thích.
b: where and when it took place
and explain why you enjoyed it
p3: Why are traditional festivals important?
Vì sao lễ hội truyền thống quan trọng?
Are festivals becoming too commercial?
Lễ hội có đang quá thương mại không?
How do celebrations differ between generations?
Cách ăn mừng khác nhau giữa các thế hệ thế nào?
p2.m: I'd like to talk about Tet, the Lunar New Year, which is the most important festival in Vietnam. The celebration I remember best was the year before last, when I went back to my grandparents' village in the north. It usually takes place in late January or February, and people spend weeks getting ready for it. That year, my whole family was there, including my aunts, uncles and cousins, so there were more than twenty of us in the house. In the days before the festival we cleaned the house, decorated it with peach blossom and made banh chung, a traditional square rice cake, which we cooked overnight over a fire. I stayed up with my cousins to watch the pot, and we spent the whole night chatting and laughing. On the first day of the new year we visited relatives and neighbours, and the children received lucky money in red envelopes. I enjoyed it so much because it was the first time in years that the whole family had been together. Normally everyone is busy with work and study, so this was a rare chance to relax and reconnect. It reminded me how important family and tradition are to me.

p2.t: Describe a difficult decision you had to make.
p2.vi: Tả một quyết định khó bạn đã phải đưa ra.
b: and explain why it was difficult
p3: Who should young people ask for advice when making decisions?
Người trẻ nên hỏi ai khi phải quyết định?
Do people make better decisions when they are older?
Người lớn tuổi có quyết định tốt hơn không?
Should children be allowed to make important decisions for themselves?
Có nên để trẻ tự quyết việc quan trọng?
p2.m: A difficult decision I had to make was whether to study medicine or computer science at university. I had to decide in my final year of high school, when I was about eighteen. My parents are both doctors, and they had always hoped I would become one too. My grades in biology and chemistry were good enough, and I knew that being a doctor is a respected and secure career. On the other hand, I had become really interested in programming. I had taught myself to build simple websites and apps in my free time, and I enjoyed it far more than anything I studied at school. The decision was difficult for a few reasons. Firstly, I didn't want to disappoint my parents, who had supported me for so long. Secondly, medicine is a very long course, so if I chose it and then changed my mind, I would have wasted years. In the end, I had a long and honest conversation with my parents. I explained why I loved computing, and to my surprise they told me they just wanted me to be happy. So I chose computer science, and I've never regretted it. It taught me that it's important to talk openly about difficult choices.

p2.t: Describe an object that is important to you.
p2.vi: Tả một đồ vật quan trọng với bạn.
b: and explain why it is important to you
p3: Why do people keep things they no longer use?
Vì sao người ta giữ đồ không còn dùng?
Do people today own too many things?
Ngày nay người ta có quá nhiều đồ không?
How has advertising changed what people buy?
Quảng cáo đã thay đổi việc mua sắm thế nào?
p2.m: I'd like to talk about an old watch that belonged to my grandfather. It's a simple silver watch with a brown leather strap, and it's probably about fifty years old. My grandfather bought it when he got his first job, and he wore it every single day until he passed away. After that, my grandmother gave it to me, because I was the grandchild who used to spend the most time with him. To be honest, I don't wear it every day, because the strap is quite worn and I'm afraid of damaging it. I usually wear it on special occasions, like family weddings or important exams, and the rest of the time I keep it in a small box on my desk. The reason it matters so much to me is not its value, because it isn't expensive at all. It's important because it reminds me of him and of the advice he gave me, especially about being patient and working hard. Whenever I look at it, I remember sitting with him in the evening while he told me stories about his life. So for me, it's not really a watch, it's a connection to my family's history.

p2.t: Describe a time when someone gave you good advice.
p2.vi: Tả một lần ai đó cho bạn lời khuyên hay.
b: and explain why it was good advice
p3: Who do young people usually ask for advice?

Why do some people not like receiving advice?
Vì sao có người không thích nhận lời khuyên?
p2.m: I'm going to describe some advice my older cousin gave me about three years ago, when I was trying to decide what to study at university. At that time, I was planning to choose business, mainly because my friends were doing it and I thought it would lead to a well-paid job. My cousin, who is about eight years older than me and works as a software engineer, sat down with me one weekend and asked me a simple question: which subjects did I actually enjoy at school? When I answered that it was maths and computers, she told me that it's much easier to work hard at something you enjoy, and that I shouldn't choose a subject only because other people were choosing it. She also suggested that I talk to a few people working in different jobs before deciding. I followed her advice, and in the end I chose information technology. Looking back, I think it was excellent advice, because I really enjoy my studies now, and my results are much better than I expected. It taught me to make decisions based on my own interests rather than on pressure from others.

p2.t: Describe a city you would like to live in.
p2.vi: Tả một thành phố bạn muốn sống.
b: and explain why you would like to live there
p3: What are the advantages of living in a big city?
Sống ở thành phố lớn có lợi gì?
Why do many young people move to cities?
Vì sao nhiều người trẻ lên thành phố?
How can cities be made better places to live?
Làm sao để thành phố dễ sống hơn?
p2.m: The city I'd love to live in one day is Da Nang, in the centre of Vietnam. I first went there on a school trip about five years ago, and since then I've been back twice with my family, so I know it reasonably well. What I like most about it is that it seems to have the advantages of a big city without many of the disadvantages. It's modern and quite developed, with good hospitals, universities and plenty of new businesses, but the traffic is much lighter than in Hanoi or Ho Chi Minh City, and the air feels cleaner. It also has a long, beautiful beach right next to the city centre, so after work you could go for a swim or a walk along the coast, which is something I can't do where I live now. On top of that, there are mountains nearby, and Hoi An, the old town, is less than an hour away. I'd like to live there because I think it would give me a better balance between work and free time. I'm hoping that, after I graduate, I'll be able to find a job there in the technology sector.

p2.t: Describe a website or app you find useful.

and explain why you find it useful
p3: Do people spend too much time on their phones?
Người ta có dùng điện thoại quá nhiều không?
What are the dangers of sharing information online?
Chia sẻ thông tin trên mạng có nguy hiểm gì?
Will online learning replace schools?
Học online có thay được trường học không?
p2.m: One app I find really useful is a map and navigation app that I use almost every day. I started using it about four years ago, when I moved to a new city to study and didn't know my way around at all. A friend recommended it, saying it was more accurate than the one that came with my phone. I mainly use it for getting around the city on my motorbike, because it shows me the quickest route and warns me about traffic jams. But I also use it to find places, like restaurants or pharmacies, and to read other people's reviews before I go. When I travel to another city, it's even more helpful, because I can download maps in advance and use them without the internet. The main reason I find it so useful is that it saves me a lot of time and stress. Before I had it, I often got lost and had to stop and ask people for directions, which was difficult in a city I didn't know. Now I feel much more confident going to new places on my own, and I would honestly find it hard to manage without it.

p2.t: Describe a lesson or class you really enjoyed.
p2.vi: Tả một buổi học bạn rất thích.
b: what you did in the lesson
and explain why you enjoyed it
p3: What makes a good teacher?
Thế nào là giáo viên giỏi?
Is it better to learn in a group or alone?
Học nhóm hay học một mình tốt hơn?
How has technology changed the way students learn?
Công nghệ đã thay đổi cách học thế nào?
p2.m: I'd like to describe a history lesson I had in my second year of high school. The topic was the ancient trade routes of Southeast Asia, which doesn't sound very exciting, but it turned out to be one of the most memorable lessons I've ever had. The teacher, Ms Lan, didn't just give us a lecture. Instead, she divided the class into small groups, and each group became a trading city with its own products, like silk, spices or pottery. We had to negotiate with the other groups to exchange goods, and every few minutes she announced events, such as a storm at sea or a new tax, that changed the rules. By the end, we understood why some cities became rich and powerful while others didn't, much better than we would have from reading a textbook. I enjoyed it because it was active and a bit competitive, and because we had to think and talk rather than just listen and take notes. It also showed me that history isn't only about remembering dates, but about understanding why people made the decisions they did. I still remember a lot of what I learned that day.

p2.t: Describe a time when you were in a noisy place.
p2.vi: Tả một lần bạn ở nơi ồn ào.
b: and explain how you felt about it
p3: What are the main sources of noise in cities?
Tiếng ồn ở thành phố chủ yếu từ đâu?
Should there be laws to control noise?
Có nên có luật kiểm soát tiếng ồn không?
Are people today more used to noise than in the past?
Ngày nay người ta quen ồn hơn xưa không?
p2.m: I'm going to talk about the time I went to a big football match at the national stadium in Hanoi, about two years ago. My uncle had two spare tickets, and he invited me because he knows I'm a big fan of the national team. It was an important qualifying match, so the stadium was completely full, with about forty thousand people. The noise was unbelievable. From about an hour before kick-off, people were singing, beating drums and blowing horns, and when our team scored the first goal, the whole stadium seemed to shake. At times I couldn't hear my uncle even though he was shouting right next to me. At first I found it a bit overwhelming, and by the end of the match my ears were ringing. But overall I felt excited and proud, because the noise came from thousands of people sharing the same feeling. It was completely different from the noise of traffic, which just makes me tired and irritated. So I'd say it's one of the few times when being in such a noisy place was actually enjoyable, although I definitely wouldn't want that level of noise every day.

p2.t: Describe something you saved money to buy.
p2.vi: Tả một món bạn đã để dành tiền mua.
b: how long you saved for it
and explain how you felt when you bought it
p3: Should children be taught how to manage money?
Có nên dạy trẻ quản lý tiền không?
Why do some people find it hard to save?
Vì sao có người khó để dành tiền?
Is it better to save money or to enjoy it now?
Nên để dành hay tiêu ngay?
p2.m: The thing I saved for the longest was my first laptop, which I bought when I was seventeen. I needed it for school projects and for learning programming, but my parents said that they would only pay half, and that I had to find the other half myself. So I saved for about ten months. I did it in a few ways. First, I stopped buying snacks and drinks after school, which actually saved more than I expected. I also gave private English lessons to two younger children in my neighbourhood twice a week, and I put all the money from that into a box in my room. On top of that, I sold some old books and a bicycle that I no longer used. When I finally had enough money, I went to the shop with my father, and I spent almost an hour comparing different models before choosing one. I remember feeling really proud, because it was the first expensive thing I'd ever paid for with my own effort. I also took much better care of it than I would have if it had been a present, and it lasted for five years.

p2.t: Describe a tradition in your country that you like.
p2.vi: Tả một phong tục ở nước bạn mà bạn thích.
b: and explain why you like it
p3: Why are traditions important for a country?
Vì sao phong tục quan trọng với một đất nước?
Are young people losing interest in traditions?
Giới trẻ có đang mất hứng thú với phong tục không?
Should old traditions change to fit modern life?
Phong tục cũ có nên đổi cho hợp đời sống mới không?
p2.m: One tradition I really like is visiting family and friends during Tet, the Lunar New Year, which is the most important holiday in Vietnam. It usually happens in late January or February, and it lasts for several days, although the preparations start weeks before. Before Tet, families clean and decorate their homes, often with peach blossom in the north or yellow apricot blossom in the south, and they cook traditional food such as banh chung, a square sticky rice cake. During the first days of the new year, people visit their relatives, starting with the oldest members of the family, and then their friends and neighbours. When you visit someone, you wish them health and good luck, and adults give children red envelopes with lucky money. The reason I like this tradition so much is that it's the one time of year when everyone stops working and makes time for each other. My family members live in different provinces, so Tet is often the only chance I get to see some of my cousins. It reminds me of where I come from and how important family is.

para.s: The number of people cycling to work has risen sharply.
para.a: Commuting by bike has become far more popular in recent years.
w: The number of people who work in bicycle factories has risen sharply.
Cycling to work is sharply more dangerous than it used to be.
People who cycle to work have risen earlier than other commuters.
para.why: Cùng ý: nhiều người đạp xe đi làm hơn. Câu bẫy giữ từ 'risen sharply' / 'cycling' nhưng nói chuyện khác.

para.s: Children who read for pleasure tend to do better at school.
para.a: Pupils who enjoy books in their free time usually achieve higher grades.
w: Children are more likely to read when school is enjoyable.
Schools that buy more books tend to attract better pupils.
Reading at school is less pleasant than reading at home.
p: enjoy books in their free time
para.why: Ý: đọc vì thích → học tốt hơn. Câu bẫy đảo nguyên nhân – kết quả hoặc đổi chủ thể.

para.s: The museum was unable to attract enough visitors.
para.a: Attendance at the gallery remained disappointingly low.
w: The museum attracted too many visitors for its small rooms.
Visitors were unable to find the museum easily.
The museum did not want to attract more visitors.
para.why: Ít khách đến. 'unable' (không làm được) khác 'did not want' (không muốn).

para.s: Most experts now agree that the theory was wrong.
para.a: The majority of specialists have come to reject the original idea.
w: A few experts still believe the theory is correct.
Experts have always agreed about the theory.
Most experts now agree on a new theory about the same topic.
p: agree that the theory was wrong
have come to reject the original idea
para.why: 'now agree … was wrong' = 'have come to reject'. Câu 'a few still believe' có thể đúng nhưng không cùng ý.

para.s: The new bridge has reduced travel time between the two towns.
para.a: Since the crossing opened, journeys from one town to the other are shorter.
w: The new bridge took a long time to build between the two towns.
Travel between the two towns has increased since the bridge opened.
The two towns have reduced the money spent on bridges.
para.why: Thời gian đi ngắn hơn. 'Travel has increased' là nhiều chuyến hơn, không phải nhanh hơn.

para.s: Farmers were initially reluctant to try the new method.
para.a: At first, growers were unwilling to experiment with the technique.
w: Farmers were the first to try the new method.
Farmers found the new method difficult to learn at first.
The new method was initially used only on small farms.
para.why: reluctant = unwilling (không muốn). 'difficult to learn' là khó, không phải không muốn.

para.s: The company's profits fell for the first time in ten years.
para.a: After a decade of growth, the firm's earnings declined.
w: The company has made a profit every year for ten years.
The company was founded ten years ago and soon made a loss.
Profits fell for ten years in a row.
p: for the first time in ten years
para.why: Lần đầu giảm sau 10 năm. 'Fell for ten years in a row' là giảm liên tục 10 năm: ngược ý.

para.s: Using public transport is cheaper than running a car.
para.a: Taking buses and trains costs less than owning a private vehicle.
w: Public transport is more comfortable than a private car.
Running a car is cheaper in the countryside.
The price of public transport has gone up more than the price of cars.
para.why: So sánh chi phí: rẻ hơn = costs less. Câu 'price has gone up more' nói về mức tăng, không phải rẻ hơn.

para.s: The species is now found only on one island.
para.a: Today, the animal survives in a single location.
w: The species was first found on one island.
One island has more species than any other.
The species can now be found on many islands.
para.why: 'only' quan trọng: chỉ còn một nơi. 'first found' là nơi phát hiện đầu tiên.

para.s: Staff complained about the lack of training.
para.a: Employees were unhappy that they had not been taught the necessary skills.
w: Staff complained that the training was too long.
The training was cancelled because of staff complaints.
Staff were trained to deal with complaints.
p: had not been taught the necessary skills
para.why: lack of = không có. Câu bẫy giữ 'training', 'complaints' nhưng nói chuyện khác.

para.s: The government plans to ban plastic bags next year.
para.a: Authorities intend to prohibit single-use carrier bags within twelve months.
w: The government banned plastic bags last year.
The government is planning to make plastic bags cheaper.
Shops have asked the government to provide more plastic bags.
para.why: Thì quan trọng: 'plans to … next year' là chưa xảy ra; 'banned last year' đã xảy ra.

para.s: Older people are more likely to suffer from loneliness.
para.a: Isolation is a bigger risk for the elderly than for younger adults.
w: Older people prefer to spend time alone.
Loneliness makes people age more quickly.
Younger adults are more likely to visit older relatives.
para.why: Khả năng bị cô đơn cao hơn. 'prefer to spend time alone' là thích ở một mình, không phải khổ vì cô đơn.

para.s: The findings cast doubt on earlier research.
para.a: The results call into question what previous studies had concluded.
w: The findings confirm what earlier research had shown.
Earlier research doubted that the findings were possible.
The researchers doubted their own findings.
para.why: cast doubt on = call into question (khiến nghi ngờ). 'confirm' là ngược ý.

para.s: The scheme was abandoned because it was too expensive.
para.a: The project was dropped owing to its high cost.
w: The scheme became more expensive after it was abandoned.
The scheme was cheap, so it was soon forgotten.
The scheme continued despite its high cost.
para.why: Bỏ vì đắt. 'despite its high cost' là vẫn tiếp tục: ngược ý.

para.s: Few people realise how much water is used to produce food.
para.a: The quantity of water needed in agriculture is widely underestimated.
w: Few people use water carefully when they cook.
Most people know that food production uses a lot of water.
Producing food uses less water than people think.
p: how much water is used to produce food
the quantity of water needed in agriculture
para.why: Ít người biết → bị đánh giá thấp. 'Most people know' là ngược; 'less water than people think' cũng ngược.

para.s: The method has not yet been tested on humans.
para.a: Trials so far have involved only animals.
w: The method was tested on humans and failed.
Scientists do not plan to test the method on animals.
The method is not safe for humans.
p: not yet been tested on humans
trials so far have involved only animals
para.why: Chưa thử trên người (chỉ trên động vật). 'not safe' là kết luận khác: bài không nói.

para.s: Demand for the product exceeded the company's expectations.
para.a: Far more customers wanted the item than the firm had predicted.
w: The company expected demand to fall.
The product exceeded customers' expectations.
The company could not produce what it had planned.
p: far more customers wanted … than predicted
para.why: Nhu cầu vượt dự đoán của công ty. 'exceeded customers' expectations' là sản phẩm tốt hơn mong đợi của khách: khác chủ thể.

para.s: The architect drew inspiration from traditional houses.
para.a: The designer's ideas were influenced by local building styles of the past.
w: The architect designed several traditional houses.
Traditional houses were drawn by the architect as a student.
The architect wanted to replace traditional houses.
p: local building styles of the past
para.why: drew inspiration from = lấy cảm hứng. Câu bẫy dùng 'drew' theo nghĩa vẽ.

para.s: There is little evidence that the diet improves health.
para.a: Claims about the eating plan's benefits are largely unsupported.
w: There is clear evidence that the diet is harmful.
The diet has little effect on weight.
Health experts have little interest in the diet.
para.why: Thiếu bằng chứng ≠ có bằng chứng là hại. Đây là bẫy hay gặp của NOT GIVEN / FALSE.

para.s: The town's population doubled over two decades.
para.a: In twenty years, the number of residents grew to twice its original size.
w: The town's population was double that of its neighbour.
Two decades ago, the town was twice as large.
The population grew by two per cent each decade.
p: grew to twice its original size
para.why: Tăng gấp đôi trong 20 năm. 'twice as large two decades ago' là trước kia lớn hơn: ngược.

para.s: Critics argue that the policy benefits only the wealthy.
para.a: Opponents claim that the measure serves the interests of the rich alone.
w: Critics argue that the policy costs the wealthy too much.
The wealthy have criticised the policy.
Supporters argue that the policy helps everyone.
p: serves the interests of the rich alone
para.why: Người phản đối nói chính sách chỉ có lợi cho người giàu. Câu 'the wealthy have criticised' đổi người phát biểu.

para.s: The disease spread rapidly because of poor hygiene.
para.a: Inadequate sanitation allowed the illness to move quickly through the population.
w: Poor hygiene was rapidly improved after the disease spread.
The disease spread slowly despite poor hygiene.
Hygiene became poor because the disease spread.
para.why: Vệ sinh kém → bệnh lan nhanh. Câu bẫy đảo chiều nguyên nhân.

para.s: The idea was dismissed when it was first proposed.
para.a: Initially, the suggestion was rejected out of hand.
w: The idea was first proposed by someone who was later dismissed from the job.
The idea was accepted immediately.
Nobody proposed the idea until much later.
para.why: dismissed = gạt đi (không phải sa thải). Câu bẫy dùng nghĩa 'bị đuổi việc'.

para.s: Tourism has had a negative impact on the local environment.
para.a: The influx of visitors has damaged the surrounding natural habitat.
w: Tourists have a negative opinion of the local environment.
Tourism has improved the local economy.
The local environment has reduced the number of tourists.
para.why: Du lịch gây hại môi trường. 'negative opinion' là ý kiến của khách, không phải tác động.

para.s: The library is closed to the public on Sundays.
para.a: Visitors cannot use the library at weekends except on Saturdays.
w: The library is only open to the public on Sundays.
On Sundays, the library closes early.
The public library was closed on a Sunday.
p: closed to the public on Sundays
visitors cannot use … except on Saturdays
para.why: Đóng ngày Chủ nhật. 'closes early' là vẫn mở một phần.

para.s: Participants were asked to keep a record of what they ate.
para.a: Those taking part had to write down their meals in a diary.
w: Participants kept the food records for the researchers.
Participants were asked to eat what the researchers recorded.
Participants had to remember what they ate without writing it down.
p: keep a record of what they ate
write down their meals in a diary
para.why: Ghi lại món đã ăn. Câu bẫy giữ 'record', 'ate' nhưng đổi việc làm.

para.s: The device is unlikely to be available to consumers in the near future.
para.a: It will probably be years before ordinary people can buy the gadget.
w: Consumers are unlikely to want the device.
The device will soon be cheaper for consumers.
The device is no longer available to consumers.
p: unlikely to be available in the near future
it will probably be years before … can buy
para.why: Chưa sớm có bán. 'no longer available' là từng có, nay hết: khác ý.

para.s: Rising sea levels pose a threat to coastal cities.
para.a: Urban areas near the shore are endangered by the steady rise of the oceans.
w: Coastal cities have caused sea levels to rise.
Sea levels are rising faster near cities.
Coastal cities pose a threat to the oceans.
p: the steady rise of the oceans
para.why: Câu bị động đảo chủ ngữ nhưng cùng ý. Câu bẫy đổi ai đe doạ ai.

para.s: Researchers have yet to explain why the birds migrate at night.
para.a: The reason for the species' nocturnal journeys remains a mystery to scientists.
w: Researchers have explained why the birds migrate at night.
The birds migrate at night to avoid researchers.
Researchers study the birds only at night.
para.why: 'have yet to' = chưa. Hay bị đọc nhầm thành 'đã'.

para.s: The course is suitable for complete beginners.
para.a: No previous experience is needed to join the class.
w: The course is completely full with beginners.
Beginners should complete another course first.
The course is suitable only for experienced learners.
para.why: Ai cũng học được, không cần biết trước. Câu bẫy dùng 'complete' theo nghĩa khác.

para.s: The two languages share a common origin.
para.a: Both tongues developed from the same ancestor language.
w: The two languages are commonly spoken together.
The two languages share many words borrowed from each other.
One language was originally spoken by more people.
p: developed from the same ancestor language
para.why: Cùng gốc. 'borrowed from each other' là vay mượn: khác với cùng gốc.

para.s: Funding for the project was withdrawn after two years.
para.a: The sponsors stopped providing money for the scheme once two years had passed.
w: The project took two years to find funding.
Funding for the project was doubled after two years.
The project was withdrawn from the competition after two years.
para.why: Rút tiền tài trợ. 'project was withdrawn from the competition' là rút dự án, không phải rút tiền.

ln.title: Joining a sports centre
lines: Good morning, Riverside Sports Centre. How can I help you?
Hi. I'd like to become a member, please. Can I do that over the phone?
Yes, of course. I just need to take a few details. Could I have your surname first?
Thank you. And your first name?
It's 14 Mill Lane. That's in Westbury.
Mill Lane, Westbury. And a contact phone number?
Let me read that back: 07734 812 659. Lovely. Now, which type of membership are you interested in? We have standard, off-peak and family.
I think off-peak. I work in the evenings, so I'd mostly come during the day.
That's fine. Off-peak means you can use the centre before 4 p.m. on weekdays. It costs 32 pounds a month.
Oh, I was told it was 28.
It was 28 until January, but it's gone up, I'm afraid. It's 32 now.
OK, no problem. Does that include the swimming pool?
Yes, the pool and the gym are included. Classes like yoga are extra, though, 4 pounds each.
Right. And when could I start?

You'll need to do an induction first, where a trainer shows you how to use the equipment safely. The next free session is on Thursday the 9th... sorry, no, that one's full. The next free one is Friday the 10th, at half past ten.
Great. Please bring some photo identification with you, like a passport or a driving licence, so we can make your membership card.
Will a student card be OK?
No, it needs to be an official document, I'm afraid. And one more thing: how did you hear about us?
Wonderful. That means you get your first month half price. Is there anything else?
Is there somewhere to leave my bike?
Yes, there's a cycle rack next to the main entrance. You'll need your own lock, though.

qs.why: Chọn off-peak vì làm buổi tối.
Bẫy: 28 là giá cũ, giờ là 32.
"Please bring some photo identification"; thẻ sinh viên không được.

qs.s: Heard about the centre from: a ______
Bike: use the rack next to the main ______
qs.why: "a cycle rack next to the main entrance"

ln.title: Booking a day tour
lines: Hello, Coastline Tours. This is Emma speaking.
Hello. I'm calling about your day trips. I'd like to book one for next week.
Certainly. Which tour were you thinking of?
The one to the castle and the lighthouse.
That's our most popular one. It runs on Tuesdays and Saturdays. Which day would suit you?
OK. And how many people is that for?
Two adults and one child. My son is nine.
Children under twelve pay half price, so that's 45 pounds for each adult and 22 pounds 50 for your son.
That's fine. What time does it leave?
The coach leaves at 8.15 from outside the train station. Please be there ten minutes early.
Outside the train station. Got it. Is lunch included?
Lunch isn't included, but the coach stops in a fishing village where there are several cafés. Many people bring a picnic, though.
Comfortable shoes are essential, because there are quite a lot of steps at the lighthouse. And it can be windy, so bring a jacket.
OK. What else do you need from me?
Just a name for the booking and an email address. What name is it?
Oh, of course. It's Mrs Okafor. O-K-A-F-O-R.
Thank you, Mrs Okafor. And an email address for the tickets?
Lovely. If you need to cancel, please tell us at least 48 hours before, and you'll get a full refund.

qs.why: Tour chạy thứ Ba và thứ Bảy; chọn thứ Bảy.
"the coach stops in a fishing village"

ln.title: A guide to Greenway Park
ln.text: Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to Greenway Park. My name's Tom, and I'm one of the volunteers here. Before you set off, I'd like to tell you a little about the park and show you where things are on the map. The park opened in 1998 on the site of an old brick factory, and since then it has grown to cover almost forty hectares. Most of the work is done by volunteers like me. In fact, we only have three paid members of staff. People often ask how the park is funded. Some money comes from the local council, but the largest part comes from donations from visitors, so please do use the boxes near the gates. This year, our main project has been the wildlife pond. We've been removing plants that don't belong here and adding native ones, and we've already seen more frogs and dragonflies than last summer. Next spring, we're hoping to build a new adventure playground, although that depends on getting permission from the council. Now, let's look at the map. We're standing at the main gate, at the bottom of the map. If you walk straight ahead along the main path, the first building on your left is the visitor centre, where you can pick up leaflets. Just past the visitor centre, on the same side, you'll find the toilets. The café is further along the main path, on the right, opposite the toilets. It has a lovely terrace overlooking the lake. If you carry on to the end of the main path, you'll reach the lake itself, which takes up most of the top of the map. The wildlife pond I mentioned is not by the lake, as people often expect. It's in the bottom right-hand corner of the park, behind the car park. And finally, the picnic area is in the top left corner, between the woods and the lake. Please remember that barbecues are only allowed there. Right, enjoy your visit.

qs.q: The park was built on the site of
w: a farm.
a railway.
a school.
qs.why: "on the site of an old brick factory"

qs.q: How many paid staff work at the park?
w: None
Forty
Ninety-eight
qs.why: "we only have three paid members of staff"

qs.q: Most of the park's money comes from
w: the local council.
the café.
car park fees.
qs.why: Bẫy: hội đồng có góp, nhưng phần lớn từ khách quyên góp.

qs.q: This year's main project has been
w: building a playground.
planting trees in the woods.
repairing the visitor centre.
qs.why: Sân chơi là kế hoạch năm sau, còn chờ cho phép.

w: anywhere near the lake.
on the café terrace.
nowhere in the park.

qs.why: Đi thẳng từ cổng, toà đầu tiên bên trái.
Ngay sau visitor centre, cùng phía trái.
Bên phải, đối diện nhà vệ sinh.
Góc dưới bên phải, sau bãi đỗ xe; bẫy: không ở cạnh hồ.
Góc trên bên trái, giữa rừng và hồ.

ln.title: Planning a project on urban gardens
lines: So, Liam and Sofia, you've chosen urban gardens for your group project. How's the planning going?
Quite well, I think. We've decided to focus on community gardens rather than private ones, because there's more research on them.
And because we can actually visit a couple of them here in the city.
Good. What's the main question you want to answer?
At first we wanted to look at how much food they produce, but that seemed too narrow.

ln.title: Lecture: living things that make light
ln.text: Today I'm going to talk about bioluminescence, which is the ability of living things to produce their own light. Most people have seen fireflies, but in fact the majority of bioluminescent species live in the ocean. Some scientists estimate that around three quarters of the animals in the deep sea can produce light. So how does it work? In almost all cases, the light is the result of a chemical reaction. A substance called luciferin reacts with oxygen, and this reaction is controlled by an enzyme. Interestingly, very little heat is produced, which is why it is sometimes called cold light. The colour of the light varies, but in the ocean it is usually blue, because blue light travels furthest through water. Why do animals produce light? There are several reasons. The first is to find food. The anglerfish, for example, has a glowing lure on its head, which attracts small fish towards its mouth. The second reason is defence. Some squid release a cloud of glowing liquid, which confuses predators and allows the squid to escape. A third reason is communication. Fireflies use patterns of flashes to attract a partner, and each species has its own pattern. Bioluminescence is also being used by humans. Researchers have used the genes involved to study diseases, because cells can be made to glow when a certain process is happening inside them. There has even been research into using glowing plants to light streets, although this is still at an early stage, and the light is not yet bright enough to be practical. Finally, bioluminescence can tell us about the health of the ocean. Some light-producing bacteria glow less when water is polluted, so they can be used as a simple test of water quality. That's all for today. Next week, we'll look at how animals see in the dark.
